title: When Will the World End - What Religions Tell us
description:
Why do failed prophecies keep repeating across history? From Christian predictions of Jesus’ return, the Great Disappointment of 1844, and the Jehovah’s Witness Armageddon dates, to Islamic prophecies that never came true, Bhavishya Purana retrofits in Hinduism, and modern panics like Y2K and the Mayan 2012 doomsday, this video takes you on a tour of history’s most spectacular prophetic failures.

We’ll explore how cognitive dissonance explains why believers cling to failed predictions, and why the psychology of prophecy shows a consistent pattern: dates are hyped, they fail, and then the story gets reinterpreted. From Halley’s Comet scares to Heaven’s Gate suicides, from biblical timelines to astrology debunked, Pale Blue Thoughts exposes the common thread of fear, faith, and storytelling behind every failed prophecy.

#FailedProphecies #CriticalThinking #DoomsdayDebunked #ScienceOverSuperstition

This episode explains Christian failed prophecies, including Jesus’ promise in the New Testament, the Great Disappointment with William Miller, and Jehovah’s Witnesses’ moving Armageddon dates. We also dive into Islamic eschatology, hadith about the Last Hour, and the Bhavishya Purana predictions in Hinduism. Moving to the modern era, we cover the Mayan calendar 2012 scare, the Y2K prophecy panic, and Heaven’s Gate and Comet Hale-Bopp. By exploring these across religions and modern culture, Pale Blue Thoughts shows why failed prophecies, doomsday predictions, and apocalyptic cults always collapse — and why people still believe them.
